topic: Why we always see the same side of the Moon

facts.text: The discovery of fault scarp cliffs suggest that the Moon has shrunk by about 90 meters (300 ft) within the past billion years.
facts.title: Moon

facts.text: Mercury completes three rotations for every two revolutions around the Sun, a 3:2 spin–orbit resonance.
facts.title: Tidal locking

facts.text: Currently, atomic clocks show that Earth's day lengthens, on average, by about 2. 3 milliseconds per century.
facts.title: Tidal locking

facts.text: Radar observations in 1965 demonstrated instead that Mercury has a 3:2 spin–orbit resonance, rotating three times for every two revolutions around the Sun, which results in the same positioning at those observation points.
facts.title: Tidal locking
